title: Marketplace: add integration tests + fixtures for entitlement mapping and retry semantics
author: Leila Farouk
description:
Context: As part of the marketplace refresh, we’ve added an entitlement ingestion + mapping layer (AWS/GCP SKU IDs -> internal entitlements) with retries, idempotency, and audit logging. We’ve had a couple staging-only regressions where (a) duplicate webhook deliveries caused double-processing, (b) transient DB conflicts incorrectly marked entitlements as failed, and (c) AWS vs GCP payload shapes diverged without coverage. This PR adds integration-level tests and fixtures to lock down mapping behavior and retry semantics end-to-end.

What’s in this PR: (1) Golden fixtures for AWS Marketplace entitlement events and GCP Cloud Marketplace entitlement notifications (sanitized, minimal but representative). (2) Integration tests that exercise the full ingest -> validate -> map -> upsert -> audit log path, including idempotency on duplicate deliveries and deterministic retries on transient failures. (3) A small test harness to simulate backoff/retry without sleeping (fake clock) so CI stays fast. (4) Assertions on invariant fields we rely on for support/debugging: request_id propagation, entitlement_id determinism, and audit log records (created vs no-op on duplicates).

Key behaviors covered: - Mapping: AWS productCode/offer dimension + GCP planId map to the same internal plan codes as defined in the mapping table. - Idempotency: Same external event delivered N times results in exactly one entitlement activation and at most one audit log 'created' event, subsequent deliveries are 'duplicate/no-op' with stable idempotency key. - Retry: Transient errors (unique constraint conflict, network timeout to billing meter) are retried up to the configured limit; permanent errors (unknown SKU, malformed payload) are not retried and are flagged for support with an actionable error code. - Ordering: Out-of-order events (suspend arrives before activate) do not permanently wedge the entitlement; the latest effective state wins.

Notes: The fixtures include both Hosted API and Dedicated/Private examples, but they don’t assert pricing/metering values beyond ensuring the correct meter is selected. These tests run in the integration test suite using the ephemeral Postgres container and the local HTTP stub for the metering service.

Testing: - `pnpm test:int marketplace` (local) - CI: `integration-tests-marketplace` + `lint` + `typecheck`.

Follow-ups: If we keep seeing flaky failures around the metering stub, we should promote that stub to a shared helper used across billing tests (tracked separately).

conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Can we ensure we’re testing the same idempotency key derivation used in prod, not a test-only path? Also want coverage for the "unknown SKU" non-retryable classification since partner review flagged that as a frequent buyer misconfiguration.

Leila Farouk (author): Yep — the ingest helper calls the same `computeIdempotencyKey()` as the webhook handler; the test asserts on the persisted key as well. Added `unknown SKU` and `malformed payload` tests; both assert `retryable=false` and stable error codes.

Cole Summers (review): Please double-check metering stub: the retry test currently simulates a 503 then success, but does it verify we didn’t double-emit a meter event on duplicate deliveries?

Leila Farouk (author): Good catch. Added an assertion that the stub received exactly 1 `POST /meter/usage` call for the idempotency group; duplicates only produce a no-op audit record.

Chloe Martin (review): Can we add an out-of-order event test for suspend-before-activate? We’ve seen this in support tickets when buyers “re-buy” quickly.

Leila Farouk (author): Added `ordering` test: ingest suspend, then activate; final state ACTIVE with both audit entries recorded. The suspend produces a "pending" state when no entitlement exists yet.

Rafael Mendes (review): CI runtime? Integration suite can get slow. Please keep total under ~10 min.

Leila Farouk (author): Kept suite to 3 tests per provider + one retry suite; total ~2m locally and ~4m in CI on the shared runners.

Approvals: Ethan Park approved. Cole Summers approved. Chloe Martin approved. Rafael Mendes approved.
release_notes: Added integration tests and fixtures for AWS/GCP marketplace entitlement mapping; locked down idempotency and retry semantics to reduce provisioning regressions.
